plain_text:
Conservation Commission Meeting Minutes 
Public Hearing / Public Meeting Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026, Time: 7:00 PM 
Location: Searles Building, 41 Pleasant Street, Second Floor, also via Zoom 
 
Roll Call 
• Dave DiZazzo 
• Kenneth Sateriale 
• Sandra Boulay 
• Rachel Lecher 
• Mike Welch 
The above listed commissioners were present.  A quorum was confirmed.  
 
Public Hearing  
 
Notice of Intent 
A. DEP File 219-1327, MCC File 26-007 — 19 Appaloosa Drive, Eric Michel 
Israel Berl of Burrell Engineering presented the project, a septic system replacement since no 
sewer is available in the Methuen neighborhood.  The wetlands were delineated on site by a 
licensed wetland scientist, and the proposed replacement location is the only feasible site on the 
property.  The project does not increase design flow or add bedrooms.  The leaching facility is 
outside the 50-foot buffer, so no Board of Health variance is needed.  Scope includes slight 
regrading, construction of a small retaining wall along the driveway, removal of 2 trees near the 
leaching field, and installation of erosion control via composting silt socks.  Chris Parsons 
(Conservation Officer) noted the 25-foot zone encroachment is due to the wetland line being the 
tree line in an older subdivision where the area is currently existing lawn.  The Health 
Department signed off, and the permitting fee was confirmed as paid. 
Motion: Motion to close by Rachel, second by Ken.  All in favor — unanimous.  Closed.  
 
B. Abbreviated Notice of Resource Area Delineation, DEP File 219-1326 — 127 
Independence Drive, Colonial Village
Page 2 
Still awaiting peer review from Tighe & Bond; applicant requested continuance to November 
19th. 
Motion: Motion to continue to November 19th by Rachel, second by Ken.  All in favor — 
unanimous. 
 
C. Notice of Intent, DEP File 219-1320, MCC File 26-001 — 11 Cross Street, Dresser 
Williams, and Way, Inc.  Applicant requested continuance to the December 3rd meeting to 
allow time to respond to peer review comments from Tighe & Bond.  
Motion: Motion to continue to December 3rd by Sandy, seconded by Ken.  All in favor — 
unanimous.  
 
Public Meeting 
 
Acceptance of Agenda 
Motion: Motion to accept the agenda, subject to correction of a clerical error noted in old 
business item (Enforcement Order), made by Ken, seconded by Sandy.  All in favor — 
unanimous. Accepted. 
 
Acceptance of Minutes 
Motion: Motion to accept the minutes of October 15, 2026, made by Ken, seconded by Rachel.  
All in favor — unanimous. 
 
New Business 
None 
 
Old Business 
A. Stormwater Permit Application — 11 Cross Street, Dresser Williams, and Way, Inc 
Continued to the December 3rd meeting. 
Motion: Motion to continue to 12/3 by Rachel, seconded by Sandy.  All in favor — unanimous. 
 
B. Notice of Violation 24-008 / Enforcement Order 25-001 — 25 Thayer Street, Moscow 
and Cavallaro Continued from August 20/26.  Chris reported that the new homeowner, 
Mercedes Vasquez, has started installing conservation markers/posts but is having trouble, 
stating that her husband is not very handy.  Since the growing season is essentially over, the 
matter was continued to allow time for post installation. 
Motion: Motion to continue to December 17th by Rachel, seconded by Ken.  All in favor — 
unanimous. 
 
C. Notice of Violation 26-009 — 91 Lindbergh Ave, LLC Continued from September 3, 2026.  
Dennis Griecci (engineer) and the site foreman were present as representatives.  All materials 
have been removed from the 50-foot buffer and floodplain.  A 35-foot vegetated buffer is being 
established, with monitors/markers to be installed along the 35-foot line.  Wetland boundaries 
were marked, and tapes were removed to confirm clearance.  Additional wetland-type vegetation 
will be added to extend to the 35-foot mark.  Concrete (Jersey) barriers have been installed 
around all fill piles to control erosion.  Chris reported no issues and noted that conditions were 
"very good" given the amount of work completed on site. 
Motion: A motion was made by Rachel, seconded by Ken, to continue the matter to May 6, 2027 
(next growing season).  Motion carried unanimously.
Page 3 
D. Notice of Violation 26-012 — 71 Lowell Boulevard, Kathleen Becker, Patricia Howe 
Continued from September 3, 2026.  Chris reported the property had been sold to Matul Lopez.  
The new owner pulled a building permit for a 5,000-square-foot addition and cleared the entire 
site, which is in a floodplain.  The owner was notified but has not contacted the office since, 
stating an engineer was being hired to develop a plan.  Chris planned to re-establish contact the 
following morning. 
Motion: Motion to continue to November 19th by Sandy, second by Rachel.  All in favor — 
unanimous. 
 
E. Notice of Violation 26-005 — 60 Ames Street, Muhammad Tasleem.  Continued from 
October 15, 2026.  Chris reported that the property owner cut down trees and dumped brush over 
established conservation marker posts after a certified letter was delivered .  The owner called 
and, once the issue was explained, cleared everything from the resource area within hours.  As of 
the meeting, the site is in compliance, with conservation markers visible; the matter will be 
monitored into the next growing season. 
Motion: Motion to continue to May 6th by Rachel, second by Sandy. All in favor — unanimous 
 
F. Notice of Violation 26-013 — 10 Summit Ave, Carlos Vrito.  Chris reported that the owner 
wanted to cut down a large oak tree on the property.  Upon inspection, the owner had stripped 
vegetation, demolished an old deck, and moved debris from the front yard and dumped it into the 
wetlands.  However, Chris was primarily concerned about the tree.  The tree is in an existing 
lawn area within the 100-foot buffer, not in the wetlands.  A language barrier was noted; the 
owner's cousin assisted with communication, and compliance on debris removal was achieved 
within four days except for the missing conservation posts, which still need to be installed. 
Motion: Motion to continue to 11/19 by Sandy, seconded by Rachel. All in favor — unanimous  
 
G. Notice of Violation 26-015 — 8 Collier Ave, Lu Liriano.  Chris reported receiving a 
complaint about a truckload of dirt being brought in and trees being cut down.  Upon 
measurement, encroachment into the buffer zone with fill was found, and by rough measurement, 
the owner may also be encroaching onto a neighboring property.  Chris recommended that Ms. 
Liriano hire a surveyor to establish the property line before addressing other issues.  The 
applicant stated they only placed stones and gardening materials and did not believe they 
encroached upon any neighboring property.  Chris offered to informally measure the boundary at 
no cost using a tape measure (not a certified survey), with the understanding that if the applicant 
disagreed with the result, a professional surveyor would need to be hired.  Ken asked that all 
commissioners confirm agreement with this approach; commissioners indicated agreement. 
Motion: Motion to continue to 11/19, made by Rachel and seconded by Sandy.  All in favor — 
unanimous 
 
H. Enforcement Order 26-002 — 147 Hampshire Road, John DiZoglio.  Chris reported a 
complaint regarding filling/digging in the buffer zone and floodplain, where historical dirt 
mounds existed.  The property owner explained that the dirt mounds pre-dated his parents' 
ownership and were created by a previous owner who had been selling dirt; the owner had 
pushed the dirt back to its original location, not realizing new floodplain boundaries (changed 
roughly a year prior) made this a violation.  The resolution involves removing approximately 4 
inches of spread fill, identified by test samples, and installing floodplain markers.  Rather than 
standard 4x4 posts, the owner proposed planting apple trees as a boundary line marker, with the 
requirement to contact the Conservation Commission before any future tree removal in the area.  
The owner also raised the issue of tree stumps and discussed using a tub grinder to process them,
Page 4 
provided grinding stays out of the floodplain.  Chris will go to the site to confirm flagging before 
the next meeting. 
Motion: Motion to continue to December 3, 2026, by Sandy, second by Rachel.  All in favor — 
unanimous. 
 
I. Emergency Certification 26-018 — Tiffany Lane Chris reported trees leaning heavily 
toward a resident's house in the buffer zone; standard practice was applied (leave 15–20 feet, 
remove the rest). 
Motion: Motion to issue by Rachel, second by Sandy.  All in favor — unanimous.  Issued. 
 
Conservation Officer's Report 
 
• Dracut Wetland Filing Issue: Chris reported receiving calls regarding an individual in 
Dracut filing wetland delineation plans and building plans without proper credentials — 
not a professional wetland scientist, lacking a soil certificate, and using another firm's 
engineering stamp without being an employee of that firm.  Wording was proposed to add 
to the Commission's Chapter 12 procedures requiring that any individual filing plans with 
a stamp must be an employee of the stamp holder.  Legal counsel confirmed this is a 
procedural change, not requiring City Council approval, since it is a procedure rather than 
an ordinance.  This item will be placed on the next meeting's agenda for vote. 
• Forest Lake Roads Announcement: Chris shared that at a Forest Lake Association 
meeting, the mayor announced that roads around Forest Lake belong to the city (not 
unimproved ways), crediting Commissioner Mike Welch for two years of research on the 
matter; those roads are listed on the 2028 pavement improvement plan for repaving. 
• Hybrid Training Sessions: Michelle sent an email regarding training on November 30th 
and December 15th, noting DEP representatives will personally run these sessions for the 
first time.  The sessions will be available via Zoom with a slideshow presentation and a 
chat room for questions at the end.  The two sessions cover different subjects, one 
described as "boot camp" and the other focused on paperwork. 
Other Business 
Mike Welch was formally welcomed to the Conservation Commission board. 
 
Adjournment 
Motion: Motion to adjourn made by Rachel, second by Sandy. All in favor.  Meeting adjourned 
at 7:45 PM 
 
Respectfully submitted by, 
Dave Di Zazzo 
 
Approved by: 
Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary 
 
 
Submitted for the Commission:
Page 5 
Michelle Davidson, Clerk 
 
 
 
Date: ____________________
